text:
aneesa: Quick sync — product asked us to reframe the battlecard vs cloud-managed endpoints. Need two micro-angles: cost predictability and operational resiliency. Minimal jargon, field-friendly.

tom: Got it. Can we give SDRs 2 subject lines and 2 one-liners each? They want low-friction hooks.

priya: Draft subject lines: 1) "Stop surprise inference bills — 10min?" 2) "Predictable latency for customer SLAs". Short lines. A/B test both.

glen: For one-liners: (A) "We cut inference variability and keep the same models you use." (B) "Predictable latency and lower per-token unit economics for steady growth."

aneesa: Good. Also produce a 1-paragraph battle opener for the webinar: real customer, 2 charts (cost vs time, p99 tail), and 3 takeaways. Keep it <60 words.

priya: Draft opener: "A retail customer saw sudden inference bills spike 2.8x during holiday traffic. We introduced serving-first routing and prefix cache, flattening spend and restoring p99 latency — outcome: predictable margin and no code changes." Too long?

tom: Trim: "Retail client hit a 2.8x inference spike at peak. Serving-first routing + prefix cache flattened spend and stabilized p99 latency — no code changes required." That's tight.

zoe: Field objection we keep hearing: "Why not just size up instances with cloud vendor X?" Suggested rebuttal: "Sizing raises fixed costs and still leaves tail latency spikes. Our routing + cache avoids overprovisioning while protecting SLAs."

aneesa: Add a bench narrative for the brief: workload A = nightly summarization (batch-friendly), workload B = customer chat (tail-sensitive). For each, 3 bullets: baseline, what we changed, impact numbers.

glen: Workload A bullets: baseline = single-host endpoint, naive batching; change = scheduled continuous batching + quantization; impact = ~30% token cost reduction, similar output quality.

priya: Workload B bullets: baseline = customer sees p99 > 1s; change = smart routing with fallback model-variant + prefix KV cache; impact = p99 down to ~350ms and 99.9% availability during the test window.

sales-bot: quick_note: placed draft bench CSV -> https://drive.redwood/bench/1758001234/bench_summaries.csv

tom: Perfect. Aneesa, can we also give SDRs 3 short responses to "we already use vendor X":
- "Sizing is a blunt tool; we optimize serving economics instead."
- "We layer on top of your model choice, so no rip-and-replace."
- "We provide SLA-backed p99s and transparent cost breakdowns."

aneesa: Yes. Final asks: Zoe, craft the webinar CTA (single sentence). Tom, assemble subject line A/B test in the doc. Priya, paste the 2 bench narratives into /marketing/bench-briefs. Glen, make a 1-slide viz: cost delta and p99 reduction.

zoe: CTA: "See a live tail-tracer and cost model for your workload — join the webinar."

tom: I'll put A/B variants into the invite and schedule a 3-day test.

priya: Uploading briefs now. Link: https://drive.redwood/bench/1758001234/briefs.md

glen: Slide done, uploading PNG next. Method note: 10k-sample traces, synthetic peak window injected, grouping by routing policy.

aneesa: Love it. Quick timeline: final battlecard + SDR script by Wed EOD, webinar deck by Thu, playtest Fri. Thanks team.

zoe: I'll run a 5-min SDR playtest Thursday and share notes. :sparkles:
